patterns.comment: Comment line: * in column 7. Columns 1-5 are the sequence number and column 6 the form type.
patterns.name: comment.line.dds.dspf

patterns.comment: Sequence number area, columns 1-5. Not source; scoped as a comment so it recedes visually.
patterns.name: comment.gutter

patterns.comment: Anything past column 80 is ignored by the DDS compiler.
patterns.name: comment.block.line.dds

patterns.comment: Special values such as *ISO or *BLANK. Anchored to the functions area (column 45 onward); a special value cannot appear in the name or attribute columns.
patterns.name: constant.language.dds.dspf

patterns.comment: Column 7: A or O, joining this line's conditioning indicators to the previous line's with AND or OR.
patterns.name: constant.language.dds.dspf.andor

patterns.comment: Conditioning indicator 1, columns 8-10. Column 8 is N to negate.
patterns.name: constant.language.dds.dspf.n01

patterns.comment: Conditioning indicator 2, columns 11-13.
patterns.name: constant.language.dds.dspf.n02

patterns.comment: Conditioning indicator 3, columns 14-16.
patterns.name: constant.language.dds.dspf.n03

patterns.comment: Column 17, the name type. R marks a record format, H a help specification.
patterns.name: constant.language.dds.dspf.nameType

patterns.comment: Column 29: R means the field's attributes come from the file named by REF or REFFLD.
patterns.name: constant.language.dds.dspf.ref

patterns.comment: Field length, columns 30-34.
patterns.name: constant.language.dds.dspf.len

patterns.comment: Column 35, the data type and keyboard shift: A alphameric, D digits only, E DBCS-either, F floating point, G graphic, I inhibit, J DBCS-only, L date, M numeric-only character, N numeric shift, O DBCS-open, S signed numeric, T time, W katakana, X alphabetic only, Y numeric only, Z timestamp.
patterns.name: constant.language.dds.dspf.dataType

patterns.comment: Decimal positions, columns 36-37.
patterns.name: constant.language.dds.dspf.decpos

patterns.comment: Column 38, field usage. O output, I input, B both, H hidden, M message, P program-to-system.
patterns.name: constant.language.dds.dspf.usage

patterns.comment: Display line number, columns 39-41.
patterns.name: constant.language.dds.dspf.locline

patterns.comment: Display position within the line, columns 42-44. For any field after the first in a record, a plus value +n may be given instead, leaving n spaces between the end of the previous field and this one. Valid range 1 to 99.
patterns.name: constant.language.dds.dspf.locpos

patterns.comment: Argument block of the EDTCDE keyword.
patterns.name: dds.dspf.edtcde

patterns.comment: EDTCDE edit code: 1-4, A-D, J-Q and W-Z, plus 5-9 for user-defined edit codes. The optional second parameter is * for asterisk fill or an arbitrary floating currency symbol, so it is not enumerated.
patterns.name: constant.other.dds.dspf.edtcde.values

patterns.comment: Argument block of the CHGINPDFT keyword, which accepts a list of input defaults.
patterns.name: dds.dspf.chginpdft

patterns.comment: CHGINPDFT input defaults: BL blink, CS column separator, HI high intensity, LC lowercase, RI reverse image, UL underline.
patterns.name: constant.other.dds.dspf.chginpdft.values

patterns.comment: Argument block of the AUTO keyword.
patterns.name: dds.dspf.auto

patterns.comment: AUTO record advance: RA, RAB or RAZ. Listed longest-first so RAB matches before RA.
patterns.name: constant.other.dds.dspf.auto.values

patterns.comment: Colour given as the sub-expression (*COLOR value). Used by CHCAVAIL, CHCSLT, CHCUNAVAIL, MNUBARSEP, WDWBORDER and WDWTITLE, which take their colour this way rather than as COLOR(value).
patterns.name: constant.other.dds.dspf.color.values

patterns.comment: Display attribute given as the sub-expression (*DSPATR value), used by the same keywords as (*COLOR value).
patterns.name: constant.other.dds.dspf.dspatr.values

patterns.comment: Numeric literals in keyword parameters. Anchored to the functions area (column 45 onward), otherwise a digit inside a field name such as #CBX#3 is highlighted as a constant. The length, decimal, indicator and location columns have their own rules.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.dds.dspf

patterns.comment: Argument block of the CHECK keyword. CHECK accepts a list of codes, so a lookbehind anchored to CHECK( would only match the first. A container rule carries no theme colour of its own.
patterns.name: dds.dspf.check

patterns.comment: CHECK validity-checking codes: AB, ER, FE, LC, M10, M10F, M11, M11F, ME, MF, RB, RL, RLTB, RZ, VN and VNE. Longer codes are listed first so M10F matches before M10.
patterns.name: constant.other.dds.dspf.check.values

patterns.comment: Argument block of the DSPATR keyword, which accepts a list of display attributes.
patterns.name: dds.dspf.dspatr

patterns.comment: DSPATR display attributes: BL blink, CS column separator, HI high intensity, ND nondisplay, PC position cursor, RI reverse image, UL underline, MDT set changed data tag, OID operator identification, PR protect, SP select by light pen.
patterns.name: constant.other.dds.dspf.dspatr.values

patterns.comment: Argument block of the COLOR keyword.
patterns.name: dds.dspf.color

patterns.comment: COLOR names for display files: BLU, GRN, PNK, RED, TRQ, WHT and YLW. The printer file set differs; it adds BLK and BRN and has no WHT.
patterns.name: constant.other.dds.dspf.color.values

patterns.comment: Argument block of a COMP or CMP comparison.
patterns.name: dds.dspf.comp

patterns.comment: Relational operators for COMP and CMP: EQ, NE, LT, NL, GT, NG, LE, GE.
patterns.name: keyword.other.dds.dspf.comp.values

patterns.comment: Numeric literals in keyword parameters, such as SFLPAG(0009).
patterns.name: constant.numeric.dds.dspf

patterns.comment: Column 6, the form type. Always A for DDS.
patterns.name: keyword.other.dds.dspf.spec

patterns.comment: Continuation character joining this line to the next. Both + and - are valid; + discards the leading blanks of the continuation line and - preserves them. Anchored to end of line so a hyphen or plus inside a keyword parameter is unaffected.
patterns.name: keyword.other.dds.dspf

patterns.comment: Command attention and command function keys, CA01-CA24 and CF01-CF24. Anchored to the functions area so a field named CA01 is not mistaken for a command key.
patterns.name: keyword.other.dds.dspf.func

patterns.comment: Keyword set for the functions area. The first lookbehind requires at least 44 characters before the match, so a keyword is found anywhere from column 45 onward and one line may carry several. The second requires the match to begin exactly at column 45 or to follow a non-word character: a plain \b is wrong here, because a keyword starting at column 45 is valid even when column 44 holds a digit, as it does when a position entry abuts the keyword. The trailing boundary stops a keyword matching inside a longer name such as MYGDF.
patterns.name: keyword.other.dds.dspf.funcs

patterns.comment: CMP, CLRL and SFL. Held in a separate rule from the main keyword list. Anchored to the functions area so a record or field named SFL is not mistaken for a keyword.
patterns.name: keyword.other.dds.dspf.funcs

patterns.comment: A literal closes on its quote, or at the end of the line, so one missing quote cannot run on through the rest of the file. It does not close where the line ends in a minus or a plus, which the DDS reference defines as continuing the keyword and its parameter values on the next line; a minus resumes at position 45 and a plus at the first non-blank of the functions field. Blanks are excluded from the class because the sign must be the last non-blank character in the field. A comment line is consumed whole by the rule below, which leaves nothing for the end pattern to match, so a comment sitting between two halves of a literal does not close it.
patterns.name: string.other.dds.dspf.hex

patterns.comment: Continuation character ending an unterminated literal. DDS discards it and joins the lines, so it is not part of the literal's value.
patterns.name: keyword.other.dds.dspf
